assumptions: states are consistent: a non-null array begin has end >= begin and capacity covering the pairs; a callback list with a null head fn and a non-empty tail is the one inconsistent shape, and its leak behaviour is modeled exactly as observed
the model sorts with the pinned comparator; std::sort stability is unobservable here because dedup removes every duplicate pair afterwards

callback_list_drain_541cab0.note: the window calls this on the +0x98 subobject in the common teardown of both paths
callback_list_drain_541cab0.null_head: a null head fn returns immediately; tail nodes are left untouched (leaked, not freed, not invoked)
callback_list_drain_541cab0.rule: head fn at object+0x00 invoked as fn(arg at +0x08, arg at +0x10); then each tail node in +0x18 order is invoked the same way and freed with sized delete 0x20

0x5164af0.role: libstdc++ insertion sort for the pair range; shift rule pinned (shift while previous pair exceeds current pair, lexicographic arg then fn)

0x5164da0.role: libstdc++ introsort loop for the pair range; partition and pivot internals not pinned, comparator pinned as ascending (arg, fn)

census.method: per-byte E8/E9 scan over the .text file range plus a whole-file qword scan (see census.py); a regex scan would silently skip call opcodes starting inside a previous match
census.qword_slot_detail: R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocation at file offset 0x189438: slot VA 0x575b310 in .data.rel.ro holds 0x5165b80; neighbouring RELATIVE slots 0x575b308 and 0x575b318 hold 0x5164820 and 0x5164940. The owning table's class is not pinned; the window is reached indirectly through this slot, not by a direct call.

clean_path.observable_difference: array callbacks run if and only if the flag was set; list callbacks run on both paths, but on the dirty path they run before the array storage is freed and on the clean path after it
clean_path.rule: dirty flag clear: skip the sort, the dedup, the array callbacks and the inline list drain entirely; the common teardown still drains the callback list (invoking it) after freeing the array storage

common_teardown_order: free the callback-pair array storage (sized delete, size capacity_end-begin) when begin is non-null
drain the callback list via 0x541cab0 on the +0x98 subobject
drain the string list at the +0x80 sentinel
free vector C (+0x30/+0x40), then vector B (+0x18/+0x28), then vector A (+0x00/+0x10)
sized delete of the record itself, size 0xe8

dirty_flush.array_callbacks: each surviving pair invokes fn(arg) in sorted order; the call is indirect through pair+0x08 with pair+0x00 as the single argument

dedup.end_update: the deduped end is stored to +0xc8 only when it differs from the old end
dedup.rule: adjacent equal (arg, fn) pairs are removed, keeping the first occurrence; the scan compares each pair with the previous pair only, so it removes exactly the duplicates the ascending sort made adjacent

dirty_flush.flag: cleared first (movb $0 to +0xb8) before any callback runs
dirty_flush.list_predrain: the callback list is drained inline (same rule as 0x541cab0) and then the head fn at +0x98 and the tail head at +0xb0 are zeroed, so the later common-teardown drain is a no-op

callees: inline unguarded insert for elements past the first 16
sort.comparator: ascending lexicographic (arg, fn) on raw unsigned values; pinned from the 0x5164af0 insertion shift rule (shift while previous pair exceeds the current pair) and the inline unguarded insert (same rule); the introsort partition uses the same std::sort instantiation and is used by contract
sort.empty_range: begin == end skips the sort entirely
sort.threshold_bytes: 0x100 (16 pairs): at or below, the whole range goes through 0x5164af0; above, the first 16 pairs go through 0x5164af0 and the rest through the inline unguarded insert

vec_a.free: sized delete, size end-begin, skipped when begin is null

vec_b.free: sized delete, size end-begin, skipped when begin is null

vec_c.free: sized delete, size end-begin, skipped when begin is null

string_list_drain.rule: walk from [+0x80] until the node equals the +0x80 sentinel address; per node, free the string heap buffer with size capacity+1 only when the string pointer differs from the address of the node's +0x20 field (SSO inline case); then free the node with sized delete 0x30
string_list_drain.size_field_note: the string size at node+0x18 is never read by this teardown; only the pointer and the capacity are used

tree_list_drain.per_list_node: call 0x5165380 on the node's +0x18 root, then free the list node with sized delete 0x28; successor is node+0x10; a null head skips the loop

teardown_tree_5165380.rule: teardown(n): if n is null return; teardown(n.child at +0x18); delete n with sized delete 0x28; then teardown(n.successor at +0x10). Free order is children before parents, successors in order. The +0x18 descent is unrolled six levels in the binary before the recursive call; the order above is what the unrolled code implements.
teardown_tree_5165380.used_by_contract_note: the window pins the per-list-node call and the node free; the tree interior order is pinned from the callee's own disassembly, not from the window alone

unknowns: the wrapper type and the record's class name; the setter of the dirty flag and what registering a callback means for the owner
the element types of vectors A, B and C (only their byte spans are freed)
the +0x48/+0x50/+0x58 and +0x68/+0x70/+0x78 fields, the string node +0x08 field, and the tree node +0x00/+0x08 fields
the owning table behind the 0x575b310 RELATIVE slot and the roles of its neighbouring entries
whether the record is WAL-related: the window itself carries no WAL string or WAL-specific field, so no WAL attribution is claimed despite neighbouring WAL functions

window.summary: Destroys the 0xe8-byte record at wrapper+0x38. A null member is a no-op. When the dirty flag at record+0xb8 is set, the callback-pair array is sorted, deduped and invoked and the callback list is drained before the common teardown; when clear, the array callbacks are skipped and the array storage is freed before the list drain. The wrapper itself is never freed.
